grades.quote: The low-priority thread is blocking the high-priority thread by holding the mutex.
grades.reason: Directly explains how a low-priority mutex holder blocks a high-priority thread.

grades.quote: In return for that extra waiting, it guarantees that a high-priority thread will only have to loan its priority to at most one lower-priority thread to free up a needed mutex.
grades.reason: Explains a mitigation involving a lower-priority thread releasing a needed mutex, but not the underlying blocking sequence.

grades.quote: Two forms of interaction, known as priority inversion and the convoy phenomenon, are particularly interesting.
grades.reason: Identifies priority inversion as a scheduling–synchronization interaction without explaining mutex-induced blocking.

grades.quote: The function of the lock is to force other uses to wait, not to pin a piece of data to a particular agent.
grades.reason: Provides general background on lock-induced waiting, but does not address thread priorities or priority inversion.
